description: Sleep disturbance, somatic complaints, worsening of pre-existing depression or anxiety, moral distress and survivor guilt, and impaired functioning linked to compulsive news consumption and nocturnal monitoring of events.
energy_note: A diagnosis for people who were never there.

aspect: It stacks on the previous ones
description: For Iranians abroad the 2026 conflict intersects with earlier upheavals in Iran, amplifying transnational stressors through identity and kinship ties. This is not a first trauma; it is the fourth or fifth, in the same nervous system.
energy_note: Not a new wound. The same one, reopened.

aspect: Work performance falls and nobody attributes it correctly
description: The employee is up at 03:00 checking whether a district was struck, and at 09:00 in a meeting about quarterly targets. Performance management follows in due course.
energy_note: Disciplined for a war on another continent.

aspect: Collective action is the identified protective factor
description: The literature identifies diaspora mobilisation - large-scale demonstrations, organised solidarity - as what converts helplessness into agency, and communication blackouts and internal political fracture as what prevents it.
energy_note: The thing that helps is a crowd.

description: Clinicians recommend sensory grounding. It works for an acute spike and it does not address the actual problem, which is that the person's mother is in a city being bombed.
energy_note: Grounding techniques for an ungrounded situation.

description: Tehran is three and a half hours ahead of London. The strikes are at night there, which is early evening here, and the news arrives as he is putting his daughter to bed. He has done this for six weeks. She has started asking why he checks his phone during the story.
energy_note: A child learning the time difference.
